results.name: Amitābha Buddha from Hancui
results.description:
"The Amitābha Buddha or Amitabha Buddha is an enormous Buddhist statue that was originally located in Hancui village in Hebei province, northern China. Dating to the 6th Century AD, it was given to the British Museum by the Chinese Government in 1938." ~https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitābha_Buddha_from_Hancui

"A massive figure of Amitābha Buddha standing on a lotus base, made of white marble, with traces of gilding and pigments and a visible joint at the Buddha’s waist. Two hands are missing but the wooden dowels and iron brackets installed at the end of arms to hold the hands remain. Inscribed and dated." ~ http://www.britishmuseum.org/research/collection_online/collection_object_details.aspx?assetId=34168001&objectId=227481&partId=1

results.description:
# 阿弥陀三尊磨崖仏(福島県白河市)

To place Amida-Nyorai(Amitabha) in the center for the religion, and place Kannon-Bosatsu(Avalokitesvara) and Seishi-Bosatsu(Mahasthamaprapta) on both sides of Amida-Nyorai, the form is called Amaida-Sanzon(Amitabha Triad).

results.name: 阿弥陀如来坐像 / Wooden Amitabha sitting statue
results.description:
木造　一木割矧ぎ造　平安時代後期 (12世紀)　像高1.05m　東大阪市指定文化財

緩やかなカーブを描いた眉に伏した目、ふっくらとした丸い頬は優しい印象を受ける。全体的に緩やかな曲面による肉付きを表す。このような表現は、平安時代後期に京の都で流行し、地方に広がった「定朝様式」の影響を受けたもの。（引用・参考: 展示キャプション）

東大阪市長瀬にあった旧阿弥陀院の仏像として伝わり、現在は東大阪市が所有する。2023年3月まで同市立埋蔵文化財センターにて展示。その後施設閉館に伴い、現在一般の観覧ができない。文化財指定時には鎌倉時代のものとされてきた。近年の調査では、後補の影響が大きいものの平安仏の特徴をよく残す点が指摘された。また、像内には後補時のものとみられる、浄土宗に関係のある人物の墨書が残る点からも貴重である（3Dデータでは墨書は見られません）。なお、台座は後補。

フォトグラメトリでの3D計測モデル。撮影枚数は750枚程度。撮影場所の影響で右膝部分がメッシュ化されず。承諾を得て計測し、3Dデータは2021年に市へ提供済み。

results.name: Thousand-armed Avalokiteśvara
results.description:
Figure built with Gravity Sketch VR.
Inspired by Thousand-armed Avalokiteśvara.
A Buddhist story tells of Avalokiteśvara vowing never to rest until he had freed all sentient beings from saṃsāra. Despite strenuous effort, he realizes that still many unhappy beings were yet to be saved. After struggling to comprehend the needs of so many, his head splits into eleven pieces. Amitābha, seeing his plight, gives him eleven heads with which to hear the cries of the suffering. Upon hearing these cries and comprehending them, Avalokiteśvara attempts to reach out to all those who needed aid, but found that his two arms shattered into pieces. Once more, Amitābha comes to his aid and invests him with a thousand arms with which to aid the suffering multitudes.

results.name: Maitreya, the Buddha of the Future
results.description:
Stele of Maitreya Buddha, 563 CE, in the collection of the Minneapolis Institute of Art.

 From the sculpture's description on artsmia.org:
 "In addition to the central Maitreya image with its incised halo and flanking bodhisattvas, apsaras and dragons appear at the top and bottom of the flame-shaped mandorla. The small figures on lotuses at the feet of the bodhisattvas represent the new souls being born in the Western Paradise of Amitabha Buddha. The neatly carved sixty-nine-character inscription on the rear of the stele names the donors who commissioned the piece and had it dedicated in 563."
 
 More information about the sculpture here:
 https://collections.artsmia.org/art/61570/stele-of-maitreya-buddha-china

results.name: 12th C CE Water-Moon Guanyin - point cloud
results.description:
Twelfth-century Water-Moon Guanyin, now in the collection of the Minneapolis Institute of Art.

From the sculpture’s description on artsmia.org:

"This form of the bodhisattva presides over his own paradise, Potolaka, which is described in scripture as a rugged seaside cave from which Avalokiteshvara could admire the reflection of the moon in the water. Appropriately, he appears meditative and relaxed and is seated informally in the “royal-ease” posture. Ornately dressed, with silk robes, fluttering sashes, jewelry, and an elaborate hairstyle, he also wears a headpiece that features an image of Amitābha, the buddha to whom Avalokiteshvara attends. Believers might look to a sculpture like this as a guide for their own journeys toward enlightenment."

The sculpture on Mia’s website:

https://collections.artsmia.org/art/32122/seated-guanyin-china

The mesh version of the object is here:
https://skfb.ly/68PAA
